summary.title: Omni-WorldBench: Towards a Comprehensive Interaction-Centric Evaluation for World Models

details: Existing world-model evaluations measure visual fidelity / text-video alignment (FID, FVD, VBench) or static 3D geometric consistency (WorldScore, whose only 'interaction' is camera motion), leaving the core world-model capability — how interaction actions drive state transitions in space and time — unmeasured.

Omni-WorldBench, an interaction-centric benchmark for 4D video world models, consisting of Omni-WorldSuite (a prompt suite organized along a three-level hierarchy of interaction scope: effects confined to the acting object, object-to-object local effects, and multi-object/global environment change) and Omni-Metric (an evaluation protocol whose core is interaction-effect fidelity).

Score the causal effect of the prescribed action on both final outcome and intermediate state trajectory: revisit-frame long-horizon consistency (InterStab-L), motion energy of non-target regions (InterStab-N), VLM-verified per-entity affected/unaffected behavior (InterCov), and VLM-verified ordering of key events (InterOrder).

Heterogeneous dimensions are fused by an agent-based aggregator: an MLLM reads the prompt semantics, ranks the importance of interaction fidelity vs. video quality vs. camera-object controllability, and maps the ranking to weights yielding a single AgenticScore.
1,068 prompts, each = text description of interaction-driven state evolution + initial frame, plus a camera trajectory for a subset (return-to-origin / loop-closure cases included).
Dataset-grounded route: first frames + recorded camera trajectories from DriveLM (driving), InternData-A1 (robot manipulation), Sekai (gaming), captioned by Qwen-VL and human-verified.

Concept-driven route: prototype taxonomy of scene/object/action per interaction level, prompts and trajectories generated by ChatGPT-5.2 and cross-checked by Gemini and DeepSeek-R1, first frames from FLUX.1-dev (3 candidates, CFG 3.5, 50 steps, >=1024x1024) with Qwen-Image refinement and human screening.
Per-prompt metadata: affected vs. unaffected entity lists with expected motion direction/magnitude, temporally ordered key-event list, expected camera motion and revisit frames.
Multi-label annotation over physics principles, commonsense, causality, camera motion, loop-closure consistency, spatial constraints; Level 2 is the largest interaction-level bucket.
Structured extraction: GroundingDINO+SAM entity mask trajectories, RAFT optical flow, flow-derived relative camera motion.
Video quality reuses VBench imaging quality, temporal flickering, motion smoothness, dynamic degree, plus WorldScore content alignment; camera control reuses WorldScore rotation/translation error.

New/modified: Object Control reframed as per-object binary VQA over uniformly sampled frames (replacing rule-based detection matching); Transitions Detect uses PySceneDetect ContentDetector giving binary 1 if no scene cut.

InterStab-L = mean of grayscale SSIM and CLIP-feature cosine over annotated revisit frame pairs, with a static-anchor gate zeroing trivially static videos; InterStab-N = exp(-normalized mean flow magnitude in non-target regions).

18 models across three paradigms: T2V (Director3D, OpenSoraPlan, T2V-Turbo, HunyuanVideo); IT2V (Matrix-Game2.0, Wan2.1, Wan2.2, CogVideoX-5b-I2V, OpenSora v2, Cosmos-predict-14B, LargeVideoPlanner); camera-conditioned (HunyuanWorld v1.5, Hunyuan-GameCraft, ViewCrafter, Gen3C, Lingbot, FantasyWorld, WonderWorld).
Diffusion-based, autoregressive, and hybrid generators, each run with its official codebase settings on NVIDIA H20 GPUs.
T2V and IT2V models evaluated on 410 prompts; camera-conditioned models on a dedicated 120-prompt subset with explicit trajectories.
15 metrics across the three dimensions; dimension scores are simple averages of sub-metrics before MLLM-weighted aggregation into AgenticScore.
Qualitative case studies on a Level-2 throwing interaction and a Level-1 left-strafe camera trajectory.

key_findings.finding: Current video world models are near-saturated on conventional video quality yet clearly deficient in interaction fidelity, exposing a gap between visual realism and true interactivity.
key_findings.evidence: Across the 18 models, temporal flickering and motion smoothness mostly exceed 95%, while Interaction Effect Fidelity averages range only from about 42% (Matrix-Game2.0, ViewCrafter) to 67.34% (Wan2.2); InterCov and InterOrder sub-scores are typically in the 35-65% range.

key_findings.finding: The image-conditioned (IT2V) paradigm currently leads overall interaction-centric performance, with Wan2.2 the best model on the benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: AgenticScore: Wan2.2 75.92% and Cosmos 75.42% (IT2V) versus best T2V HunyuanVideo 73.96% and best camera-conditioned HunyuanWorld 74.36%; Wan2.2 also tops IT2V interaction fidelity at 67.34%.

key_findings.finding: Adding explicit camera control induces a strong trade-off between camera accuracy/long-horizon revisit consistency and stability of non-intervened scene content.
key_findings.evidence: WonderWorld attains 96.12% camera control and 84.96% InterStab-L but only 24.89% InterStab-N; ViewCrafter reaches 81.15% InterStab-L with 4.22% InterStab-N; Hunyuan-GameCraft scores just 27.96% camera control with 50.08% interaction fidelity.

key_findings.finding: Dynamic degree, not temporal smoothness, is the principal axis of variation among models, and high dynamism often coexists with degraded interaction consistency.
key_findings.evidence: Dynamic degree spans 16.83% (OpenSoraPlan) to 100.00% (ViewCrafter, WonderWorld); Matrix-Game2.0 has 99.02% dynamic degree yet the lowest interaction fidelity average (42.76%) and the lowest AgenticScore (60.33%).

key_findings.finding: Qualitative failure modes corroborate the interaction-fidelity metrics on the hierarchical prompts.
key_findings.evidence: On a Level-2 throwing prompt, Wan2.2 produces a coherent complete pitching motion while Matrix-Game2.0 shows temporal collapse and disappearance of the human figure; on a Level-1 left-strafe camera prompt, ViewCrafter hallucinates a spurious building whereas HunyuanWorld remains stable, matching their respective scores.
